author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Forty-eight Manchester students earned New Hampshire’s Seal of Biliteracy in 2026, contributing to the program’s largest statewide cohort since it launched five years ago.

Manchester Ink Link reported that 533 students across New Hampshire received the distinction this year. Because some demonstrated proficiency in more than one additional language, the state issued 547 awards. Languages represented included Spanish, French, Portuguese, Arabic, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Chinese and American Sign Language, among many others.

The seal recognizes graduating students who meet English requirements and demonstrate intermediate-level proficiency in listening, speaking, reading and writing in another language. Approved assessments include Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate and other state-recognized language tests. Recipients receive a seal on their diploma, a state certificate and a graduation cord.

The Manchester group shows how the recognition is reaching students in the state’s largest school district. State education officials describe multilingual ability as useful for community connections and future work. New Hampshire also recognized 48 middle-school students with a Junior Seal of Biliteracy, extending the program’s pathway to younger learners.
dek: Forty-eight Manchester students earned the state distinction as New Hampshire recognized its largest annual cohort since the program began.
headline: Manchester students help New Hampshire Seal of Biliteracy reach record
